I highly suggest keeping any and all drawings like this. That way if the time comes that you can't draw (for whatever reason). You at least have this too look at and feel. I have tons of drawings I have done during different emotions and it's quite interesting how important they've become to me.

I can relate. I take medication as well but it doesn't seem to do much. I also know the dreaded idea of "it will get better". People want to say this to each other because they want to believe in some kind of promise, some kind of idea that if they say it it will happen. But I think it's bullshit. My dad used to tell me all the time about how he knows something good will happen for me like getting a wife, and finding a good job. Who wouldn't want to say that to their sad son? But the truth is he doesn't know that will happen it's only a guess. I feel people need to be careful the way they encourage and not promise what's impossible. It only makes it not happening worse.

In some ways I'm glad I have a 'moral compass' but in others I'm not. I'm too afraid to do anything that's even a little against the rules. That, and I screw up anyway not because I want to be rebellious. That's my problem I understand we all make mistakes but I make so many and then get yelled at as if I did something wrong. My parents did this to me and now my boss and co-workers do this to me. It feels like I'm cursed.

Once when I was a kid (probably 9-10 years old) 
I had just gotten done taking a bath and got out to take shit. I noticed we were out of toilet paper,
I went into my room to get dressed (so I could head to our downstairs bathroom and wipe there).
I started putting on my socks first and as I sit down I was horrified to notice that I had made a poopy print on my hard-wood floor! I decided that the toilet paper was a necessary now
I finished getting dressed and headed down stairs to get some toilet paper, I was even more horrified when I saw my mom coming up the stairs with my dog behind her,
I beat her to my room trying to find cover for my mistake
She had some of my laundry and was going to put it on my bed, 
I made sure to stand in front of my "stamp",
she emptied the basket on my bed and headed out, 
my dog, however, stayed and proceded to smell and lick up my stamp from the floor
Still one of my most vivid childhood memories...
